lead: An array a program nests in a loop can end the process inside the `Core` member that reads it, with no diagnostic at all.
body: A member converting an array into a Rust tree recurses once per level, so twenty thousand wraps printed `has overflowed its stack` under debug and release alike — not the parser's clean refusal, which only covers a deep *literal*. Probe an attack's nesting step with `target/debug/nvs.exe run` first, and bound the member the way `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/db/schema.rs`'s `DEPTH_LIMIT` does.
